name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_SEQ_Q01 - Sequence of processes in recombinant DNA technology

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following major steps of recombinant DNA technology in the correct chronological sequence:

(I) Ligation of the desired DNA fragment into a vector
(II) Isolation of the genetic material (DNA)
(III) Transferring the recombinant DNA into the host
(IV) Fragmentation of DNA by restriction endonucleases

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Recombinant DNA technology follows a strict operational workflow from obtaining pure genetic material to introducing the engineered construct into a host organism.

Step 2: Chronological Ordering
First, pure DNA must be isolated from the source organism free from other macromolecules. Second, the isolated DNA is fragmented at specific recognition sites using restriction endonucleases. Third, the desired DNA fragment is ligated into a cut cloning vector using DNA ligase to form recombinant DNA. Fourth, the recombinant DNA is transferred into a suitable host cell for multiplication and expression.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is Isolation of DNA \(\rightarrow\) Fragmentation by restriction endonucleases \(\rightarrow\) Ligation into a vector \(\rightarrow\) Transfer into the host, which corresponds to (II) \(\rightarrow\) (IV) \(\rightarrow\) (I) \(\rightarrow\) (III).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_SEQ_Q02 - Sequence of steps in DNA isolation and spooling

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps involved in isolating pure DNA from a cell in the correct order:

(I) Addition of chilled ethanol to precipitate DNA
(II) Treatment with ribonuclease and protease to remove RNA and proteins
(III) Breaking open the cell using enzymes such as lysozyme, cellulase, or chitinase
(IV) Removal of separated DNA threads by spooling

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To cut DNA with restriction enzymes, it must be extracted in pure form, free from cell debris, RNA, proteins, polysaccharides, and lipids.

Step 2: Chronological Ordering
First, the cell wall and membranes are broken open using appropriate lytic enzymes (lysozyme for bacteria, cellulase for plants, or chitinase for fungi) to release DNA along with other macromolecules. Second, contaminating RNA and proteins are removed by treating the lysate with ribonuclease and protease, respectively. Third, chilled ethanol is added to precipitate the purified DNA out of solution. Fourth, the fine threads of precipitated DNA are collected and removed by spooling.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is Cell lysis \(\rightarrow\) Removal of RNA and proteins \(\rightarrow\) Precipitation with chilled ethanol \(\rightarrow\) Spooling, which corresponds to (III) \(\rightarrow\) (II) \(\rightarrow\) (I) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_SEQ_Q03 - Sequence for bacterial competence and heat-shock transformation

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps for transforming bacterial cells with recombinant DNA via the heat-shock method in the correct sequence:

(I) Placing the cells briefly at \(42^{\circ}\text{C}\) (heat shock)
(II) Treating bacterial cells with a specific concentration of divalent calcium ions
(III) Putting the cells back on ice
(IV) Incubating the competent cells with recombinant DNA on ice

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Because DNA is hydrophilic, bacterial cells must first be rendered competent and then subjected to a temperature shift to take up recombinant plasmid DNA.

Step 2: Chronological Ordering
First, bacterial cells are treated with a specific concentration of a divalent cation such as calcium to increase DNA entry efficiency through cell wall pores. Second, these competent cells are incubated with recombinant DNA on ice. Third, the mixture is placed briefly at \(42^{\circ}\text{C}\) to deliver a heat shock. Fourth, the cells are immediately placed back on ice, completing the uptake of recombinant DNA.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is Calcium ion treatment \(\rightarrow\) Incubation with rDNA on ice \(\rightarrow\) Heat shock at \(42^{\circ}\text{C}\) \(\rightarrow\) Returning cells to ice, which corresponds to (II) \(\rightarrow\) (IV) \(\rightarrow\) (I) \(\rightarrow\) (III).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_SEQ_Q04 - Sequence from DNA elution to downstream processing

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following events in the correct order from DNA fragment recovery to final product marketing:

(I) Elution of separated DNA bands from the agarose gel
(II) Staining separated DNA with ethidium bromide and exposure to UV light
(III) Large-scale culturing of transformed cells in a bioreactor
(IV) Downstream processing including purification and preservative formulation

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Recovering a target gene fragment for cloning and subsequently producing its protein product on an industrial scale follows a defined multi-stage workflow.

Step 2: Chronological Ordering
First, DNA fragments resolved by agarose gel electrophoresis must be stained with ethidium bromide and exposed to UV radiation to visualise bright orange bands. Second, the desired DNA band is cut out and extracted from the agarose gel piece by elution. Third, after ligating the purified fragment into a vector and transforming the host, cells are cultured on a large scale in a bioreactor to express the recombinant protein. Fourth, the biosynthetic product undergoes downstream processing—separation, purification, formulation with preservatives, and quality control testing.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological order is Ethidium bromide staining and UV exposure \(\rightarrow\) Elution \(\rightarrow\) Bioreactor culturing \(\rightarrow\) Downstream processing, which corresponds to (II) \(\rightarrow\) (I) \(\rightarrow\) (III) \(\rightarrow\) (IV).
